content:
oncall-bot: Pager: HIGH - kv-cache continuous-batching error spike in eu-west-1. Alert: latency p95 > 1.5s and 5xx rate spike across inference workers. Paging -> @mara (primary oncall).

mara: I'm on it. Seeing alerts for kv-cache memory growth + batch size amplification. Pulling metrics now.

mara: Quick context: started ~ 09:12 UTC, sustained for ~15m, coincides with traffic surge from a large customer. Several nodes showing CUDA OOM-like allocator churn in logs.

song: @mara I'm available to take a handoff if it looks like a rolling mitigation is needed.

mara: Thx @song. First checks:
- check allocator fragmentation graphs (kv_cache.arena_frag_pct)
- inspect continuous-batching config and recent deploys
- look for recent kernel/runtime changes

mara: Running `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/kv-worker --tail=200 | grep -i cuda` and scanning for `cuda malloc`/`out of memory` patterns.

mara: snippet from one node:
```
E 09:14:23 kv_worker.cpp:420 cudaMalloc returned CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
W 09:14:23 kv_cache.cpp:775 allocator fragmentation detected: arena_free=1.2GB arena_total=3.9GB frag_ratio=0.69
I 09:14:24 batching.cpp:212 batch size amplified x6 due to failed prefix cache hits
```

raj: That frag_ratio is huge. Could be our allocator arenas not being bounded after recent batch changes. Which commit shipped last deploy? @elaine can you confirm service image tag?

elaine: Deploy tag v2026.03.12-kvbatch. No infra changes in last 48h except the batch heuristics tweak merged yesterday (PR #3721) that relaxes prefix-match strictness.

mara: That matches. My hypothesis: relaxed prefix matching increased effective batchability which caused sudden larger KV cache allocations per request, increasing alloc churn and fragmentation under the CUDA caching allocator.

song: Agreed. Short-term mitigations we can try in parallel:
- Temporarily disable the relaxed prefix-match heuristic (roll config toggle) to reduce batch amplification.
- Set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` on affected pods to reduce allocator fragmentation
- Lower `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS` env for kv-worker to constrain per-request token batching
- Increase kv-cache eviction aggressiveness (lower TTL) to free prefixes

mara: I'm going to flip the config toggle to revert the prefix-match change on a small canary subset and monitor.

mara: Command I ran:
```
kubectl exec -n inference $(kubectl get pod -l app=kv-worker -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- /bin/sh -c "curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/config -d '{\"prefix_relax\":false}'"
```

mara: Canary pods switched. Observing metrics: canary p95 dropped ~350ms after toggle. Good sign.

ops-rotations: @mara if you want me to start rolling the hotfix across stable nodes I can coordinate.

mara: Yes please. @song, while they roll, please prepare a pod spec change for `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` and `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4` to deploy if frag persists. We'll need a rollout plan with one AZ at a time.

song: On it. Drafting manifest snippet:
```
env:
  - name: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF
    value: "max_split_size_mb:64"
  - name: MALLOC_ARENA_MAX
    value: "4"
  - name: MAX_BATCH_TOKENS
    value: "1024"
```

mara: Customer impact update: @customer-success-bot reports ~8 customer sessions with degraded latency, one customer reported transient 500s for 3m. No data loss, only degraded inference latencies. Ticket created: CS-4892.

elaine: Rolling config to remaining pods now. Watchlist: cpu/gpu utilization, kv_cache.heap_growth, batch_amplification metric.

mara: Rolling finished across eu-west-1. Early results: cluster-level p95 improved ~200-400ms and 5xx rate trending down.

raj: Good. But fragmentation still elevated on 3 hosts. I'd like to restart the kv-worker process on those nodes to free GPU allocator state (safe action, will cause short-lasting connection restarts). Thoughts?

song: Restarting should free CUDA caches. Do it one host at a time and notify CS for potential short disruptions.

mara: I'll cordon one node and restart pod. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-worker -n inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=ip-10-0-4-23` (one node only)

mara: Restart done on node ip-10-0-4-23. Logs after restart show allocator recovered, frag_ratio down to 0.22. p95 on that node back to baseline.

ops-rotations: Rolling restarts scheduled for the other two affected hosts with 5m gap.

elaine: After restarts and config roll, aggregate metrics show memory churn reduced and amortized batch size returned to expected distribution. No new 5xx in last 12m.

mara: Preliminary RCA notes for postmortem:
- Trigger: recent batch heuristic (PR #3721) increased effective batchability under a traffic surge from large customer -> magnified per-request KV cache allocations.
- Root cause: allocator fragmentation exacerbated by unbounded glibc arenas and CUDA caching allocator fragmentation; we lacked automation to bound arenas and tune `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` preemptively for high-batch workloads.
- Mitigations applied: reverted prefix-relax config; set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` and `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4` on affected pods; sequential restarts to flush CUDA caches; lowered `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS` temporarily.

song: Follow-ups to schedule:
- Backfill automated chaos tests for batch amplification scenarios and large-customer traffic patterns.
- Add allocator health alert: kv_cache.arena_frag_pct > 0.6 -> auto-restart small pod subset and trigger pager.
- Revisit PR #3721 behavior with load testing; add a canary gating step for batch heuristics changes.

mara: I'll file the incident page and postmortem template. Assigning owners: @song for follow-up tuning, @elaine for rollout automation to set safe defaults on deploy, @raj for alerting improvements.

customer-success-bot: Notifying impacted customers: CS-4892 updated. Outreach scheduled in 1h and will include mitigation summary and ETA for final postmortem.

mara: Thanks everyone. Keeping thread open for final confirmation and postmortem.

tom: small note: add a line to run `pytorch-collector` nightly on dedicated canary to snapshot allocator fragmentation metrics monthly.

mara: Good idea. Added to follow-ups. Closing operational loop once postmortem is published.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved -> status: mitigated. Please update incident severity and link postmortem when ready.
